name: mvmt_det_xgb_set85
task: binary MOVE (paretic arm) vs REST, causal, for the online VNS trigger
window_alignment: causal - the window ENDS at the current sample

sensor_roles.forearm: PARETIC forearm (a2 right / b2 left), x = forearm long axis, mounted fingers -> elbow
sensor_roles.upperarm: PARETIC upper arm (a3 right / b3 left), x = humerus long axis
sensor_roles.chest: sternum (b4), x = along the torso; mounted pointing up, which is what torso_incl_mean (~0 deg upright) assumes

sensor_sync: the three streams must be sample-aligned to within half a sample (8.3 ms)
feature_order_is_binding: booster.json and scaler.json are indexed by this order

movement_signal.name: gyr_perp
movement_signal.formula: deg2rad(sqrt(Gyr_Y^2 + Gyr_Z^2)) on the RAW (unfiltered) gyro, per sensor
movement_signal.note: x is the long axis in all three placements (regardless of which way along it the sensor is strapped), so y and z are the perpendicular axes. Stateless and orientation-free: no fusion filter, no convergence transient, and immune to dropped packets (no differentiation).
movement_signal.naming: The three features named *_vqf_speed are the long-axis angular speed; the name is kept for column compatibility with the offline pipeline and does NOT imply VQF is used - see movement_signal for how this bundle computes them.

scaler_note: NOT part of inference - XGBoost splits on x < t, so a monotone per-feature rescale is a no-op. scaler.json holds the training-set mean/scale so you can range-check the online features during bring-up.
model_format: xgboost Booster.save_model JSON, binary:logistic, outputs P(MOVE)
decision_rule: p_smooth = mean of the last 3 window probabilities (fewer at a segment start)
while ARMED, the first window with p_smooth >= threshold starts a stim_ms stimulation
no new trigger during the stimulation or the lockout; re-arm once p_smooth < threshold
reset every filter/VQF/smoother/arm state across gaps > max_gap_ms
threshold_selection: the only tuned decision parameter. Median of the 16 LOSO thresholds chosen by loso_smoothed(target_precision=<our VQF's mean point-wise precision on these windows, 0.745>) inside each fold's inner LOSO; folds agreed to within 0.67-0.70. Window geometry and k were fixed a priori to match the baseline, not tuned.
notes: Feature definitions: src/windows_features.py::build_windows (_sensor_signals + _window_features). That is the spec; this config only pins the geometry, order and coefficients around it.

Per sample: acc_free = acc - R(quat)^-1 * [0,0,9.81] (Xsens onboard quat, world Z-up), computed BEFORE the 20 Hz low-pass. The raw-acc 0.5-20 Hz bandpass in preprocessing.filter_imu feeds no SET85 feature - skip it online.

Movement signal (gyr_perp): deg2rad(sqrt(Gyr_Y^2 + Gyr_Z^2)) on the RAW (unfiltered) gyro, per sensor. NO magnetometer is used anywhere in this bundle - every feature is derived from the quaternion, the accelerometer and the gyroscope only. The three features named *_vqf_speed are the long-axis angular speed; the name is kept for column compatibility with the offline pipeline and does NOT imply VQF is used - see movement_signal for how this bundle computes them.

windows_features smooths elevation/flexion with scipy uniform_filter1d(size=5), which is CENTRED: it peeks 2 samples (33 ms) ahead. This affects elev_speed_*, flex_speed_*, elev_rom, flex_rom (12 of the 85). Online, lag those channels by 2 samples or accept the mismatch. It is the only non-causal step in the extractor.
Filters are causal scipy sosfilt started from zi = zi_unit * first_sample (steady state), which is what preprocessing.apply_filter/apply_lowpass do.

booster.json stores learner_model_param.base_score as a PROBABILITY; the intercept added in margin space is its logit. A hand-written tree walker must use logit(base_score), and must not read the intercept off pred_contribs (that column is the SHAP expected value, a different number). p = 1 / (1 + exp(-(sum of leaf values + logit(base_score)))).

Reset the filter states, the probability smoother and the armed/firing state across any data gap > max_gap_ms; and drop a window whose samples span more than (window_samples-1)/rate_hz + 100 ms of wall clock.

training_data.refit_note: refit on ALL subjects; the numbers below are the LOSO estimates from models trained on n-1

event_level.rule: 1 s burst + re-arm, TP = >=300 ms of the burst inside a movement
